definition: A corner is the cut, where two card edges meet. It is not the printed frame. Rounding is the arc past the measured 10–90% edge rise. The radius comes from the tip setback and from a circle fit to the silhouette. They must agree within 0.1 mm. The hinge is image-top. A corner is read from the scan in which that corner faces image-bottom, rule 2026.10.13-shadow-free-v1. Top corners come from the 180 scan. Bottom corners come from the upright scan. The other scan stays on the sheet. A setback inside the scanner limit, with missing area under 0.20 mm², is a result, reported as sharp with that limit stated. The limit is the larger 10–90% rise of the two edges at that corner. Radius 0 is not published. A corner that is not a clean arc publishes the area of card missing as the primary measure and the setback from the ideal corner point as the secondary measure. Missing area repeats across the two scans. The hinge moves the color crossing, so the setback does not. It does not publish a radius. Whitening is paper showing against the same border at mid-edge, read on the same clear scan as the corner. Whitening on a border that is already paper-white is not applicable. A pale patch that is foil glare is withheld. A ding is a local notch in the cut. It is read on the same clear scan as the corner. Fraying is fiber outside the fitted cut. It is read on the same clear scan as the corner. A card-colored strand counts when it runs at least 0.3 mm. A pale or tan fiber counts when it continues past the scanner rise and that beard runs at least 0.20 mm along the corner. One missed sample does not break the beard. The outward walk reaches 2.0 mm. It used to stop at 0.85 mm, which published a longer hair as 0.840 mm. Length 0 means neither is present. The clean controls set that floor: their longest pale speck is 0.05 mm. Softness is how far along the cut, from the tip, the face 0.22 mm or 0.40 mm inside the cut fails to match that same edge. The edge color is the median of samples every 0.2 mm from 10 mm to 14 mm. The longer run is published, in millimetres. A short length means the corner matches its own edge. It is a result. No soft cutoff is assigned. A side the centering key has withheld does not grow a corner grade. TD-12 is excluded. TD-14 through TD-21 are an unapproved worn and control review. TD-18 and TD-21 are the clean controls. Flatbed backs of TD-01 through TD-11 and Karros are a separate unapproved corner review. The two BGS slabs are reference labels only. They stay sealed, stay out of the answer key, and are an order check between corners 9.5 and corners 9. A quad that is not card-sized, or an unclear step with no missing card, stays withheld. Unapproved until the owner checks the overlay. No 0–10 corner score is assigned. This review does not change grading.

orderCheck.rule: Once a corner method exists, a corners 9.5 should not measure worse than a corners 9.
orderCheck.families: White-border Score and foil Momentum. This pair is an order check. It does not set a millimetre scale.

calibrationProposal.note: After the worn fronts exist and the owner has approved the overlays, submit six raw cards: TD-01 and Karros (sharp on all four corners), TD-02 (a fitted radius on one orientation), and three worn cards that carry a soft corner, a ding, and fraying. The first six stay with those white-border and worn cards. Foil, the halftone Pokémon card, and the full-bleed card wait. If the six corner subgrades fall on one half-point, stop.

phone: A phone corner is not scored. It waits until those two edges already match the centering key, on a still in the ±0.1 mm tier (at or above 30 px/mm) or the ±0.2 mm tier (from 15 px/mm up to 30).
